plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of silvery-green shrubs turn into ribbons of violet-blue. The slender flower spikes hum with bees and give off a sweet, herbal perfume that carries across the countryside.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, with peak bloom around mid-July
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest of all the proteas, with a dinner-plate-sized flower head. Its crown of silky-tipped pink bracts surrounds a core of tiny true flowers. It blooms on rocky fynbos hillsides in the middle of the southern winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, June to October
plants.location: Western Cape fynbos, South Africa (for example around Cape Town)
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. The plant belongs to an ancient family that dates back to the supercontinent Gondwana. Its thick underground stems help it regrow after wildfires.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, cupped, fragrant flowers rise on tall stems above round, water-repellent leaves. They open at dawn over the still water of ponds and paddies, and are a classic sight of high summer in temperate Asia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, from around June or July through August
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across temperate East Asia, including Japan and China
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic waxy texture that makes water bead up and roll off, carrying dirt with it. Scientists call this the 'lotus effect' and have copied it in self-cleaning coatings.
